title: Something More Terrifying Than Death
text: That day at noon, Panda, Éclair, Fiancée, and the others who were in the neighboring town got introduced to Arc and his group through Father, I say. I also saw them coming and going from Doctor’s laboratory, among other places. Around evening, they came to the kitchen and helped Father prepare dinner. Meanwhile, I was busy playing around with Ho-kun.
“I thought a god-slayer would be some more amazing kind of existence, but you’re pretty normal, huh.”
“Raph.”
Keel asked Arc without any hesitation whatsoever.

“I’m happy to hear you say that. I go around calling myself a god-slayer, which sounds grand, but honestly speaking, it’s more like a self-proclaimed executioner who cracks down on people overstepping their bounds and causing trouble for other worlds.”
Arc answered with a smile. From just today alone, I could tell that he was an extremely gentle-natured person, indeed.

“You should be careful about looking down on and mocking that cat there—if you do, you might end up wishing you were dead instead of what he’ll do to you. He acts humble, but calling him ‘self-proclaimed’ is honestly too modest for the monster he really is. Because of guys like that, that cat there has suffered a whole lot of trouble.”
Ho-kun butted in there with some teasing commentary.
“So like, karmic retribution incarnate for those guys?”
“You don’t have to say something so scary, do you? Besides, it’s more of a hassle if you put that bird there in a bad mood.”

“Fufufu, right now I happen to be in a good mood, you know. I’ve been in a good mood for about three hundred million years now. Even after being pestered by Motoyasu-kun all day today, it hasn’t wavered!”
“No, you need to have some self-awareness that your units of time are messed up.”
Three hundred million years is quite a long stretch to stay in a good mood, I say.

“When was it again? There was that time you got mad at some parasite mooching off another world—kept repeating half-baked reincarnations while keeping its memories even after dying—and you rewrote things so it’d keep reincarnating as plankton until it did it properly.”
“……What bird are you, doing the same thing as that guy?”
“Eh, is it really such a bad thing to encourage some thoroughly rotten soul to reflect a little?”
“Well…… by our standards, we can’t really call it cruel since it was the one causing harm.”
“Indeed, that’s true.”
Reincarnators are basically a menace as a general rule. Just like Takt, thinking of the ones still scheming in the shadows of the world, there’s hardly a decent one among them, I say.
“There are exceptions here and there, though. Unapproved reincarnations tend to rot the soul, generally speaking.”
“Is that so, indeed?”
“Ah, in the case of you heroes, it’s different, so you can rest easy. There’s a spirit-approved avoidance of death worked into it—seems like you never actually died in the first place.”
Oh! So I wasn’t dead after all! I’d just gotten a stamp of approval from Ho-kun himself.
“I see, understood!”
“Your reply’s awfully lively, isn’t it, you.”
“Good match for that bird there. Go do your comedy duo routine together, being from the same world and all. Forever.”
“Ah! That’s so mean! If we’re bringing that up, that cat there once turned some immortal jerk doing whatever he pleased into a lump of meat and left him like that until the end of the world!”
“I was just teaching him that there are things more painful than destruction in this world. For a lowlife getting carried away with his immortality and spreading countless sorrows around.”
“What kind of devil are you, seriously…… Still, seems like there’s a whole universe’s worth of things more terrifying than death out there.”
Father was showing a certain degree of understanding there, I say. Right as they were having this conversation, Older Sister came over carrying a bottle of liquor.
“Ohh, Naofumi-chan and everyone—Older Sister wants in too!”
Slightly tipsy Older Sister began pouring drinks for Father and the others.
“Let’s toast to celebrate meeting Arc-chan and everyone! Come on, drink up, drink up!”
“Sadeena…… you really are something.”

Father drank, looking exasperated at Older Sister’s antics. She poured moderately for Big Sister, but generously for Father, Arc, and Ho-kun. Ah, this must be it—Older Sister’s baptism, I say. She was gauging just how much they could drink, if they could drink at all.
“Ah, this goes down smooth.”
“The proof’s subtly high, though.”
Arc and Ho-kun gulped down the poured drinks one after another.
“Ugh…… she’s making them drink dragon-slaying liquor, nano. No mercy at all, nano.”

Rival was recoiling from a distance, visibly disturbed—quite a memorable sight, I say. Apparently the drink Older Sister was serving had a strong effect of getting dragons drunk. But Arc and Ho-kun kept drinking whatever was poured for them without a care in the world.
“I think this is better than nectar, honestly.”
“That stuff has kind of an arrogant taste to it sometimes, doesn’t it. The real thing goes down much smoother, and there are so many soma knockoffs floating around too, which is a pain.”
“The scale of what you two are talking about is just wrong on every level.”
“Naofumi-chan, there’s this too!”
Older Sister held out a whole cluster of lucor fruit to Father.
“Ah.”

Father plucked one of the lucor fruits and popped it into his mouth. This was something of a unique skill only Father could pull off, I say. Apparently, if anyone else tried the same thing at some other tavern, the people around would recoil and the mood would sour instantly. Older Sister seemed genuinely pleased that Father could eat these lucor fruits. Even now, she still watched him do it with a dreamy look on her face sometimes.
“Ah, lucor, huh. Come to think of it, this world has them too.”
Arc plucked a berry with a little pop and tossed it into his mouth, chewing away just like Father had.
“Ohh……”

Older Sister’s face showed genuine surprise. If I recalled correctly, Older Sister’s type was someone who could hold their liquor better than she could. The candidates other than Father had just suddenly multiplied, I say!
“You can eat these too? They’re good, right?”
“Of course. Lucor fruit’s been around since ages, ages ago. Shows up in other worlds sometimes too.”
“It’s that old a thing?”
“Yep.”
Ho-kun also plucked one with a pop and started eating. In-in-indeed, as expected of god-slayers, I say. It was startling to see people besides Father who could eat them without issue.
“Y-you don’t get drunk?”
Big Sister asked Arc timidly.
“That’s right. I don’t get drunk.”
“Me neither. Well, that cat there not getting drunk is a different matter, but I’ve got this whole incarnation-of-fire aspect going on, so alcohol’s more like fuel to me, if anything.”
Ohh, so Ho-kun was saying that alcohol just burns up as fuel for him. Sort of like a car, perhaps?
“It’s more like your personality is permanently drunk to begin with.”
“Ah, you’re going there? That’s harsh.”
“I see. So that Sadeena over there prefers guys who can hold their liquor better than she can. She’s been coming on strong at me, but this should help spread the attention around a bit.”
“Ohh, Naofumi-chan, how mean! The very first person who could out-drink Older Sister was Naofumi-chan, so there’s no wandering eye here—I’m devoted, you know!”
“Feel free to wander.”
“No waaay! Older Sister thinks Arc-chan and Ho-chan are wonderful and all, but she’s not switching away from Naofumi-chan!”
“Kya!” Older Sister squealed, getting all excited beside Father.
“Ahaha. Full of energy, aren’t you.”
“We’ve both got wives already, so we’ll leave that cat to you.”
“Indeed.”
“No waaay!”
“Haha, you two suit each other much better anyway, Naofumi-kun.”
Arc said, gently steering things back toward Father with a warm smile.
“By the way, speaking of lucor fruit episodes I know of…… there was this incredibly hard-drinking demon girl who once used it to give herself the courage to confess to a boy she had a crush on.”
“Confessing with liquid courage, huh.”
Arc rested his chin on his elbow, eyes closed, smiling as if lost in a fond memory.
“They used to be enemies, those two, but I’m glad it worked out happily for them……”
“Enemies of a god-slayer? People falsely claiming to be gods?”

“Mm…… no, this is about people who stopped me back when I’d gone completely off the rails. It’d be rude to compare them to those self-proclaimed god types—they’re good kids. I owe who I am now to them, so I’m grateful.”
“Arc-san, off the rails……”
I agreed wholeheartedly with Big Sister’s opinion there. Given how gentle-natured he was, it was hard to imagine him ever having gone off the rails at all, I say.
